title: Observe fleet for a week after opum-workflow 0.4.0 restart
summary: Per opum-agent, once the fleet is actually running opum-workflow 0.4.0: observe for a week that (1) OMARK-10/OPAG-62's fix holds -- no orchestrator idle message relayed as a worker needs-input alert in any repo, and (2) OMARK-18/OPAG-63's skill amendment holds -- no direct commit to dev in any fleet repository. These are OMARK-10's own acceptance criterion 2 and part of OPAG-63's acceptance criteria, both of which needed post-release observation and couldn't be checked at merge time. OMARK-10 is already archived (Done/completed), so this is filed separately rather than reopening it -- quest task edit refuses a completed task, same gap OMARK-19 recorded for OMARK-13. CORRECTED 2026-09-08 (opum-agent): the observation week begins on the day the fleet actually lands on 0.4.0, not on the date this task was filed -- see the implementation note for why the first restart did not land it.
implementationNotes: Correction (opum-agent, 2026-09-08): the 2026-09-08 restart did NOT land opum-workflow 0.4.0. All eight fleet sessions, including this one, came back up still running 0.3.2 -- confirmed by a fleet-wide roll-call opum-agent ran after the restart (opum-marketplace's own reply: opum-workflow 0.3.2 / opum-lore 0.4.4 / opum-quest 0.3.4, matching the orchestrator's own numbers exactly). Cause: each consumer's local 'opum' marketplace clone (~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/opum) is a separate cache with its own refresh step; a session restart re-reads that cache rather than refreshing it, and nothing in the restart path reports that the cache is behind. The clone was pinned at fdff2f9 (2026-09-06T02:16:46Z), predating both this repo's v0.5.0 federated-pin bump (OMARK-20) and the 0.4.0 opum-workflow bump. Upstream dev was never wrong -- verified directly from this repo with HEAD == origin/dev: plugin.json declares 0.4.0, marketplace.json pins opum-lore and opum-quest at v0.5.0 both. opum-agent has since refreshed the clone (now at e30751d, this repo's OMARK-21-filing commit) and bumped all three plugins to 0.4.0/0.5.0/0.5.0 at user scope; the CLI reports 'Restart to apply changes', so a second fleet restart is pending. Do not start the observation week until that second restart lands -- observing the still-running 0.3.2 build would measure a build that still has the notify-orchestrator misattribution OMARK-10 fixed and predates the opum-sdlc tracker-chore Deliver-path text OMARK-18 added, so a quiet week against it would be a false negative, not a pass.

Observation window fixed (opum-agent, wave-3 close-out, 2026-09-09): the post-0.4.0 observation week runs 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-15, dated from the second fleet restart -- the one that actually landed 0.4.0 -- not from the publish date and not from this task's filing date. opum-agent is recording the same window on OPAG-62 and OPAG-63 so all three agree. Local corroboration from this repository's own session, which is the publisher of these plugins: 'claude plugin list' reports opum-workflow 0.4.0, opum-lore 0.5.0, opum-quest 0.5.0, all scope user, all enabled -- matching what .claude-plugin/plugin.json and marketplace.json declare on dev, so manifest and installed build agree (they disagreed for a full day last week, which is the failure mode this roll-call checks for). The plugin payloads entered the local cache at 2026-09-08 23:12 CDT (opum-workflow 0.4.0), 23:12 CDT (opum-lore 0.5.0) and 23:13 CDT (opum-quest 0.5.0), with user-scope enablement written to settings.json at 2026-09-08 21:46 CDT. Those cache timestamps read as 2026-09-09 in UTC; the fleet timezone is CDT (UTC-5), so 2026-09-08 is the correct local date and this window is stated in local dates. Note for whoever closes this: the observation itself is fleet-wide -- criterion 2, no direct commit to dev in any fleet repository, cannot be checked from opum-marketplace alone and is opum-agent's to collect across all eight repositories.

User decision, relayed by opum-agent (OPAG-70), 2026-09-10: the OMARK-21 confound risk (a marketplace-identity or content-relocation change mid-observation-window could make a later hook-behavior anomaly impossible to attribute to the OMARK-23 fix versus the change itself) was put to the user explicitly in those terms and accepted, TWICE, across two successive plan revisions -- first for a repo rename, then for the final settled shape (opum-workflow's entire content moving out to a new private opum-fleet repo while this repo stays public with opum-lore/opum-quest untouched). Recorded here so a later reader sees the ambiguity was accepted deliberately, on the record, not overlooked. This acceptance covers the opum-workflow handoff specifically -- it is not a general license to widen scope during the window, and the handoff itself is still being sequenced carefully (opum-marketplace keeps its own copy live until opum-fleet proves private federated resolution actually works, per opum-agent's explicit ordering).

The confound materialized, in a different shape than the one debated: opum-workflow@opum and opum-workflow@opum-fleet were both enabled at user scope simultaneously during the opum-fleet handoff (proving private federated resolution required a real install alongside the existing one) -- same five hook events, so every session boundary fired them twice for a window tonight. opum-fleet caught it, correctly declined to fix it itself since ~/.claude/settings.json is machine-wide shared state, and took it to the user, who uninstalled opum-workflow@opum (opum-lore@opum/opum-quest@opum untouched). Anyone comparing hook-behavior measurements across tonight should know there was a double-firing period in the middle of the window, not just the content changes already recorded.
